subject: FintechCo — regional pricing follow-up & volume qualification
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@fintechco.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:21:00 -0800
Subject: FintechCo discovery recap — volumes, regional residency, and next steps

Hi Sophie / Oliver —

Great to speak earlier today. Quick recap to make sure I captured your needs and the next steps on our side. Please correct anything I’ve mis-stated.

Summary of what you shared:
- Current pilot: ~5M generated tokens/month (chat + prompting) with a small test for embeddings (~0.5M ops/month).
- Planned ramp: 25M tokens/mo in 6 months, 100M tokens/mo in ~12 months (growth driven by productizing the assistant across two product lines).
- Traffic split: ~55% US, ~45% EU (EU residency required for EU customers; logs and model inference must remain in-region for those requests).
- SLA: 99.9% availability target, and sub-200ms p50 for simple prompt paths is preferred.
- Procurement: approximate budget window and timeline: decision & PO in ~4–8 weeks.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of <= $1,200 per 1M tokens as a helpful reference number.

Questions we still have / validation items from your team:
1) Can you confirm whether the EU residency requirement applies to embeddings as well as generative calls?
2) For the 100M ramp case, is a reserved-commit (dedicated) pricing approach something you would consider?
3) Any hard constraints on contract length or preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly vs annual)?

What we’ll do next (action items from Redwood):
- I’m attaching a preliminary pricing estimate (Redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx) that breaks down list-hosted pricing vs. committed/dedicated pricing and shows the impact of EU-hosted requests (+regional uplift).
- Also attaching a short data residency summary (Data-residency-summary.pdf) that explains how we isolate EU traffic, routing options, and what logs are retained in-region.
- Marissa (cc’d) — can you lead a short SRE/SE call to review the latency SLOs & the dedicated capacity options later next week?

Proposed next step: quick 30-min follow-up with Sophie + Oliver + Marissa next Wed (Nov 25) to walk the estimate and procurement options. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: Redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 tab overview), Data-residency-summary.pdf (2 pages)

Subject: Re: FintechCo discovery recap — volumes, regional residency, and next steps

Thanks Dylan — this looks right. Couple clarifications inline: 

- EU residency: yes, applies to all inference for EU customers including embeddings and logs. EU traffic must be processed and stored in EU infrastructure.
- Volumes: pilot = 5M gen tokens / month today. We expect to hit ~25M tokens/mo within 6 months after we finish Phase 1 rollout, and ~100M tokens/mo after a year if adoption goes well. Embeddings are currently ~0.5M ops/mo with potential to grow to ~5M within 12 months.
- Budget target: to be transparent, our finance team is modeling a target of approximately $1,000–$1,200 per 1M tokens as the threshold for greenlighting a large committed deal. If list-hosted pricing is materially higher we’ll need to look at a dedicated/commit model.
- Procurement timeline: we’re hoping to have commercial terms & PO in the 4–8 week window you noted.

Next steps: Wed Nov 25 at 11:00am CET / 2:00am PST is tricky for us — can we do 10:00am CET (1:00am PST) or push to Thu Nov 26? We’ll try to join whatever is most convenient for the Redwood SE.

Also can you attach SOC2 evidence and any data residency attestations? I’ll share those with our security and procurement teams.

Best,
Sophie Chen
Head of Product, FintechCo
S: +44 7700 900111

Subject: Re: FintechCo discovery recap — regional pricing estimate (US vs EU)

Sophie — thanks for the quick confirmation and the timeline. Attached the spreadsheet I mentioned with three scenarios (pilot, ramp, and 100M committed): Redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx. High level summary here so your finance team has something to react to quickly.

High-level pricing / unit economics (examples):
- Hosted API (no commit) — US region list price: $1,500 per 1M tokens (generation). EU-hosted requests: +15% uplift to cover regional infra & compliance footprint => $1,725 per 1M tokens. Embedding ops priced separately in the sheet (lower per-op cost; see tab).
- Committed / Dedicated capacity — for predictable high-volume customers we offer committed discounts. Example: a 12-month commit at 50M tokens/mo equivalent can reach ~$1,000 per 1M tokens effective (US region), and EU-hosted requests would carry the same regional uplift if served from EU-dedicated pools. Exact numbers depend on commit size and burst allowances.
- Cost drivers / levers: intelligent batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles typically reduce effective billed tokens and lower the per-1M effective cost by 10–30% depending on your workload mix. We’ve included a sample sensitivity table in the spreadsheet.

Quick example (rounded):
- Pilot (5M/mo, hosted): list estimate ~ $7,500/mo (US-weighted).
- Ramp (25M/mo, mixed US/EU): blended list estimate ~ $34k/mo (before committed discount and caching efficiencies), EU portion increases blended unit cost by ~7–10% depending on precise split.
- Committed 50M+ monthly: effective pricing can approach $1,000 per 1M tokens with a formal commit (see sheet).

Next steps / proposed meeting:
- Marissa (cc) — can you run through the latency SLO feasibility and dedicated sizing during the SE call?
- Sophie / Oliver — would you prefer an initial SE call focused on technical fit or jump straight into a commercial review with procurement + legal? We typically do a joint session (SE + commercial) to speed things up.

I’ll also attach our SOC2 attestation and the data residency one-pager for your security team (SOC2-attestation.pdf).

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx, SOC2-attestation.pdf, Data-residency-summary.pdf
